This module introduces no new CFR (Code of Federal Regulations) citation and no new external
source. It's pure synthesis — placing a clause module 4 already quoted in full against a process
`quality-system-essentials` already taught in depth — so no new sourcing was needed or attempted
this session.

Beyond those, the external links below were each checked on 2026-11-11 and cover sub-topics
(supplier change notification, quality agreements, configuration change control) that this
module only touches. None is HIPAA-specific, and none is used as a source for any claim in the
lesson itself.

**External links:**

- **[Pharma Supplier Qualification: Audits, Quality Agreements, Change Control & Supply Chain Controls](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xkg4bmOdsVk)**
  (GMP Scenarios, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. Industry
  training content on pharmaceutical supplier qualification, not blood- or IT-specific. Watch it
  to see change control and quality agreements treated as one connected system. Verified
  embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Contract Manufacturing Arrangements for Drugs: Quality Agreements Guidance for Industry — FDA](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/contract-manufacturing-arrangements-drugs-quality-agreements)**
  FDA's own guidance page on written quality agreements between a drug owner and a contract
  facility. It is drug-manufacturing guidance, not blood or IT, but it is the regulator's plain
  statement of why responsibilities, including change handling, belong in writing. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Supplier-Change Management for Drug-Product Manufacturers — BioPharm International](https://www.biopharminternational.com/view/supplier-change-management-drug-product-manufacturers)**
  An industry trade-press article on how manufacturers handle supplier-initiated changes: what
  agreements typically require and how notices feed the buyer's own assessment. Read it for the
  "supplier change notice" vocabulary this lesson's clause discussion parallels. Verified loading
  via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Working with Supplier Change Notifications (QMS) — Veeva Vault Help](https://quality.veevavault.help/en/gr/54469202/)**
  A software vendor's help page showing how a quality system can receive a supplier's change
  notice and route it into the customer's own change process. It is product documentation, not a
  standard; read it as an illustration of the workflow. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).
- **[SP 800-128, Guide for Security-Focused Configuration Management of Information Systems — NIST](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/128/upd1/final)**
  NIST's guide to controlling and assessing changes to systems from a security standpoint,
  including security impact analysis. Useful for the impact-assessment step of your own change
  control. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[SP 800-161 Rev. 1, Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations — NIST](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/161/r1/final)**
  NIST's guidance on managing risk from suppliers and subcontractors, the broader frame for why
  a vendor's own changes and its own suppliers matter to you. Large; skim it rather than read it
  through. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[How to Review a Vendor Contract — Venminder](https://venminder.com/blog/how-review-vendor-contract)**
  A third-party-risk vendor's plain-language walkthrough of what to look for in a vendor
  contract. A commercial blog, so treat it as practitioner perspective, not authority. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

**Internal links, not external sources:**

- **[Business Associate Agreements](../business-associate-agreements/index.qmd)** — module 4. The
  full, verbatim text of 45 CFR 164.314(a)(2)(i)(C) and 164.504(e)(2)(ii)(C) — the incident-
  reporting clause this module builds its reactive-vs-proactive distinction on — lives there, quoted
  from `sources/cfr/45-164-business-associate-excerpt.md`. This module deliberately doesn't re-quote
  it at length; go back to module 4 for the full paragraph and the complete (e)(2)(ii)(A)–(J)
  checklist walkthrough.
- **[Change control for regulated systems](../../quality-system-essentials/change-control-for-
  regulated-systems/index.qmd)** — `quality-system-essentials`, module 4. The five-stage process
  (request, impact and risk assessment, approval, implementation, verification) that governs changes
  to Lakeshore's own BECS (Blood Establishment Computer Software) and eQMS (electronic quality
  management system) is taught there in full and referenced, not redeveloped, here. Read it (or
  re-read it) for the mechanics this module assumes you already have.
- **[Reading an ISO 27001 Certificate](../reading-an-iso-27001-certificate/index.qmd)** — module 3.
  Its Statement of Applicability finding on the vendor's plausible "change management" control
  domain is the internal-governance half of this module's central distinction; this module's other
  half is the contractual-notice question, which that domain doesn't answer.
- **[Investigating a Healthcare Data Incident](../../healthcare-security-and-privacy/investigating-
  a-healthcare-data-incident/index.qmd)** — the closed incident this course has used as its running
  example throughout, and the source of the root-cause finding (the deployment-sequencing gap) this
  module's change-notification discussion is built to address going forward, without reopening or
  altering that course's own final determination.

If a future session wants to verify this module's reasoning against a real AICPA, ISO, or HHS
(Department of Health and Human Services) source, the relevant sourcing notes are already recorded
in modules 2–4's own `resources.qmd` files and in this course's plan file
(`plans/vendor-and-third-party-risk-management.md`) — nothing further was fetched for this closing
module.

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about vendor change notification and fourth-party risk.

- **[How Do You Handle Fourth Parties at Your Critical Vendors?](https://venminder.com/blog/handle-critical-vendors-fourth-parties)** (Venminder — vendor/commercial content) — short guidance on monitoring your vendor's vendors and asking for notice in contracts. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Fourth-party risk management: What you need to know](https://www.vanta.com/resources/how-to-manage-fourth-party-risk)** (Vanta — vendor/commercial content) — explains fourth-party exposure and which changes (subprocessors, regions) are worth being told about. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Reassessing Risk: The Move to Third-Party Management](https://www.isaca.org/resources/isaca-journal/issues/2024/volume-6/reassessing-risk)** (ISACA Journal, 2024) — argues that point-in-time reviews miss change and makes the case for ongoing, risk-based monitoring. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM): Concepts and Mitigations](https://destcert.com/resources/supply-chain-risk-management/)** (Destination Certification) — CISSP study page covering ongoing supplier monitoring and contractual requirements; supports CISSP Domain 1 (and touches Domain 7 on change management). Commercial training site. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
